description: Place the USER'S OWN image file on the canvas: a picture they generated, a product shot, their logo. Give exactly one source: url (a direct https link to the file; the server fetches it, refuses private or local addresses, follows at most 3 redirects and checks the real type from the bytes), data_url (base64; practical only for small files, because every character is output you must write), or asset_id (from POST /api/v1/assets, which is how a shell agent uploads a local file with one curl; see the reply's next field). PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF up to 4 MB land as an image in the box exactly like place_image (fit cover crops through a clipPath, contain fits whole, corner_radius, scrim for overlay text). An SVG up to 512 KB and 1500 elements is sanitised (scripts, event handlers, external links and foreignObject removed) and imported as EDITABLE shapes fitted into the box and grouped; as:"image" keeps it as one picture instead. Without width and height it keeps its natural size, shrunk to fit and centred on the artboard. Coordinates are local to artboard when given. One undo step. The reply carries layout_src ("asset:<id>", valid 24 h) to reuse the same raster as an image node or photo_card src in create_layout without sending it again. Never use this to smuggle in SVG you wrote yourself: build artwork with the drawing operations. SVG typed inline as a data_url is refused, and SVG files that read as model-written are refused too. The one exception is purpose:"pattern_tile": a small repeating tile (patterns, textures, hatching, dot fields; at most 128 units a side) that becomes a repeating pattern fill on shape_ids, never a picture on its own. For stock photography use search_photos.

as.description: SVG only: shapes (default, editable) or image (one picture). Rasters are always images.

asset_id.description: ast_... from POST /api/v1/assets or an earlier upload_asset reply. Expires after 24 h.

data_url.description: data:image/png;base64,... (or image/svg+xml). Small files only; use asset_id for anything over a few KB.

purpose.description: artwork (default): place the user's file. pattern_tile: an SVG tile that repeats as the fill of shape_ids (patterns and textures only).

scrim.description: Images only: a gradient wash so text over the picture reads.

shape_ids.description: pattern_tile only: the shapes to fill with the repeating tile.

tile_size.description: pattern_tile only: the tile's width in document units (height follows the SVG's aspect). Default: the SVG's own width, capped at 128.

url.description: Direct https link to a PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or SVG file (not a web page).

name: upload_asset
title: Upload image or file
